summary.headline: Mitsu Chem Plast Q2 FY27 PAT rose 224% YoY to Rs 610.47 lakhs on 12.41% EBITDA margin; revenue up only 3.67%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 9,580.87 lakhs, up 3.67% YoY, while EBITDA rose to Rs 1,188.55 lakhs at a 12.41% margin and PAT reached Rs 610.47 lakhs (6.37% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 19,095.40 lakhs (+7.46% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 2,738.03 lakhs (14.34% margin) and PAT of Rs 1,484.30 lakhs (7.77% margin). Management said the strategy is margin-first, with a shift toward higher-margin niche products, and pointed to IBC entry and a Rs 1,000 crore revenue ambition by FY28 without giving a build-up. Management gave no firm IBC revenue, capex or margin figures, and EBITDA margin was about 3.5-4 points lower QoQ.

segments.name: Industrial packaging
segments.commentary: Management put it at about 81.88% of revenue for the period and called it the core business; analysts said it was broadly flat, and management described a very slight dip with focus shifting to higher-margin items.

segments.name: Hospital furniture parts (Furnastra brand, launched 2025)
segments.commentary: About 16.27% of revenue. Management said niche items are now above 16% of mix, up from 13-15%, and about 30% YoY growth; exports are being developed in 18 registered countries.

segments.name: Infrastructure furniture and others
segments.commentary: About 1.86% of revenue. Management called the sales seasonal and said the decline was not a concern.

guidance_outlook: Management targets Rs 1,000 crore annual revenue by FY28. It gave no build-up and said details would be announced shortly; the current run-rate is about Rs 400 crore.
Management said revenue at optimal utilisation from existing capacity is about Rs 425 crore, and said practical utilisation is 85-90%.
The 1,000-litre IBC facility in Khalapur is expected to be operational in Q3 FY27, with most of the impact in Q4. Management said IBC margins will be higher than the core, without quantifying.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 demand to be strong and says the EBITDA margin is sustainable, with improvement targeted but not quantified.
Management said exports should begin commercially this year, after trials and approvals.
capex_capacity: Four facilities with 58 blow moulding machines and 22 injection moulding machines; capacity above 36,000 MTPA.
Average capacity utilisation about 64% in FY26 (one answer said 63%), and about 50%+ on average per another answer; the figures given were inconsistent.
Fully automated Khalapur facility for 1,000-litre IBCs, expected operational in Q3 FY27. Capital turnover about 15x vs 8-10x for other products. Capex amount and IBC capacity were not disclosed.
Management said no further capex beyond the IBC project is planned for now.
demand_pricing: Management said overall demand is very good, with one or two industries down and the rest strong.
Exports go to USA, Canada and Europe; exports were about 1.5% of revenue in H1 FY27 per management.
Management said realisations should rise under a cost-plus model, but volume growth was not quantified. Management said the focus is on profitability over volume.
Polymers are not hedged; about 90-95% of raw material is bought domestically. Reported margins include no inventory gains.
Management said West Asia tensions have not affected export projects or orders so far.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Rs 1,000 crore FY28 target square with a current run-rate of about Rs 400 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a build-up, saying more plans would be announced soon. It said the target is a basket of plans, not mainly IBC, and that it had not said the capacity was enough without capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall QoQ by about 3.5-4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, that double-digit EBITDA is good in the current market, and that it is working to improve further. It did not give a number for the quarter-on-quarter dip.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth, given flat-to-weak revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were stable to slightly up and that low-margin portfolio items were rationalised in favour of higher-margin products, without giving volume figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is IBC on track, and what revenue and margin will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IBC will start in Q3 (through December), margins will be higher than the core, and it would give no revenue or market-size numbers until production begins.

qa_highlights.question: What are H1 vs H2 revenue split and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is generally about 40% and H2 about 60% of annual revenue. FY26 utilisation was about 63-64%, and practical maximum is 85-90%, which would mean about Rs 400-420 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company outsourcing any production?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some production is outsourced depending on market conditions, but the share is not considerable and no percentage was given.

risks_watch: FY28 Rs 1,000 crore target looks far from the current run-rate of about Rs 400 crore, and no build-up was given.
IBC start (Q3 FY27), revenue, capex and margins are still undisclosed, and the facility had not started by the call date.
Revenue growth of only 3.67% YoY in Q2 against a large EBITDA gain; the margin dipped QoQ.
Cash balance of Rs 6.07 lakhs against borrowings of Rs 9,648.44 lakhs, with D/E at 0.76x; higher depreciation and interest from new capex could weigh on PAT.
Export commercial revenue is still small (about 1.5% of H1 revenue); exports to Poland and new approvals are yet to show in numbers.
Utilisation figures given on the call were inconsistent (about 50%+, 63%, 64%).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and margins, but evasive on quantification: it gave no numbers for IBC revenue, margin, capex, market size or the FY28 target, deferring to a later announcement.
key_quotes: Our ambition is to achieve Rs. 1,000 crores in annual revenue by FY '28.
I think double digit EBITDA is a good in this kind of market scenario.
Our fully automated Khalapur facility for 1,000-liter IBC container is expected to be operational by Q3 FY 2027.

adds.what: Fully automated Khalapur facility for 1,000-litre IBCs (capacity not disclosed)

growth.why: Management targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue by FY28 (about 2.5x the ~Rs 400 crore run-rate) with no build-up, backed only by the Khalapur 1,000-litre IBC plant due in Q3 FY27 (capacity and capex undisclosed) and ~64% utilisation on ~Rs 425 crore existing capacity.
